research_mode: official Home Office accredited statistics; fail-closed limitations; no parcel score, candidate value or business result

sources.name: Court data provider
verified_claims: Court proceedings data are supplied by the Crown Prosecution Service Counter Terrorism Division and cover completed cases from year ending March 2011 to March 2026.
limitations: The series covers completed court cases rather than all arrests.

sources.name: Sentence-length data gap
verified_claims: Sentence-length breakdowns for defendants tried and convicted after March 2024 are excluded because the data were unavailable to the Home Office.
limitations: The missing breakdown limits sentence trend analysis.

sources.name: Conviction-rate historical rank
verified_claims: The 93% conviction rate was the second highest for a year ending March since comparable records began in March 2010.
limitations: Historical rank is conditional on cases tried and not a general crime rate.

sources.name: Principal-offence basis
verified_claims: Court data use the principal-offence basis, showing the most serious offence with the largest sentence when a person is tried for multiple offences.
limitations: Counts therefore do not represent every charge or offence in a trial.

sources.name: Section 58 convictions
verified_claims: Section 58 of the Terrorism Act 2000 had 17 convictions, the largest listed principal-offence count.
limitations: Principal-offence counts omit additional offences in multi-offence trials.

sources.name: Section 2 convictions
verified_claims: Section 2 of the Terrorism Act 2006 had 10 convictions for dissemination of terrorist publications.
limitations: This court aggregate cannot identify local public-safety conditions.

sources.name: Section 5 convictions
verified_claims: Section 5 of the Terrorism Act 2006 had 8 convictions for preparation of terrorist acts.
limitations: The count is national court data, not a parcel risk score.

sources.name: Schedule 7 convictions
verified_claims: Schedule 7 of the Terrorism Act 2000 had 7 convictions as the principal offence.
limitations: Principal-offence statistics must not be interpreted as incident locations.

sources.name: Custody record high
verified_claims: The 273 persons in custody on 31 March 2026 was the highest total since comparable records began and exceeded the previous peak of 267 at 31 December 2025.
limitations: Custody levels are system-wide and not local exposure measures.

sources.name: Custody ideology categories
verified_claims: Of the 273 in custody, 159 were categorised as Islamist-extremist, 80 as Extreme Right-Wing and 34 as Other ideologies.
limitations: Institutional ideology categories must not be used to profile communities, individuals or parcels.

sources.name: Terrorist prisoner releases
verified_claims: Forty-one terrorist prisoners were released in the year ending 31 December 2025, compared with 50 in the previous year.
limitations: Release totals are national and do not identify release destinations or local risk.

sources.name: Release sentence mix
verified_claims: Of 41 releases, 17 had sentences under four years, 21 had sentences of four years or more, none were released from IPP or life sentences, and 3 had been convicted but not sentenced.
limitations: Sentence history does not identify an individual's destination or parcel-level risk.

sources.name: Other-force development status
verified_claims: Section 43 search and arrest figures for forces outside the MPS are published as Official Statistics in Development because of identified data-quality issues.
limitations: These figures should not be used for precise force-to-force or parcel comparisons.

sources.name: Schedule 7 examinations
verified_claims: There were 2,614 Schedule 7 examinations in Great Britain, 14% more than the 2,290 in the previous year.
limitations: Examinations are not arrests or convictions and do not measure parcel risk.

sources.name: Schedule 7 biometrics
verified_claims: Fifty-three percent of UK Schedule 7 examinations involved at least one biometric identifier, covering 1,436 persons out of 2,714 examinations.
limitations: The UK denominator differs from the Great Britain examination total and must not be mixed without care.

sources.name: Schedule 7 strip searches
verified_claims: Eight strip searches were carried out under Schedule 7 powers in the year ending 31 March 2026.
limitations: A small national procedural count cannot support local inference.

sources.name: Air freight examinations
verified_claims: There were 566 air freight examinations, 41% fewer than in the previous year.
limitations: Freight examinations are operational activity and not parcel-level public-safety evidence.

sources.name: Sea freight examinations
verified_claims: There were 302 sea freight examinations, 92% more than in the previous year.
limitations: The national change does not describe risk at a property.

sources.name: Schedule 7 solicitor access
verified_claims: There were no refusals to postpone questioning for solicitor consultation and three instances of delayed solicitor access.
limitations: Procedural safeguards data are not measures of neighbourhood safety.

sources.name: Other-force missing-data limitations
verified_claims: For non-MPS section 43 records, 5% had the reason for a resultant arrest recorded as not stated and 19% had self-defined ethnicity not stated or missing.
limitations: The missingness varies between forces and prevents precise demographic or parcel-level comparisons.
